newsitem.title: USA: Dade Cty Mayor vetoes muni underwriting syndicate.
newsitem.headline: Dade Cty Mayor vetoes muni underwriting syndicate.

text.p: Florida's Metropolitan Dade County Mayor Alex Penelas on Friday vetoed the selection of a team of bond underwriters for an upcoming aviation deal, citing "serious concerns" regarding allegations of unethical conduct by Smith Barney Inc, a unit of Travelers Group Inc, and other firms.

Smith Barney is currently under investigation for a 1994 Dade County Water and Sewer Authority bond offering in which Smith Barney and Howard Gary & Co served as co-senior managers, Dade County said in a statement.
Smith Barney spokesman Bob Connor in New York City declined to comment, but said the firm would release a statement in response to the move later Friday.
The SEC investigation has focused on a savings presentation made to Dade County and certain fees received by the firm as a result of that transaction, the county said.
Penelas said in statment that until investigation is concluded, there are sufficient grounds to exclude Smith Barney from transactions with Dade County.
On Feb 25, 1997, the Metro-Dade Commission selected a team of underwriters, which included Smith Barney, as the underwriters for the refunding of Aviation revenue bonds.
The veto is the first by Penelas, who was the first to be elected mayor since Miami adopted the strong mayor form of county government that established the mayoral veto last year.
The Metro-Dade Commission can override the Mayors veto by a two-thirds vote of commissioners present at the next regularly scheduled meeting set for March 18.
If no override occurs, a new team of underwriters would be selected by the Metro Commission.
Penelas said that the veto comes at a time when the Dade County Bond Finance program is under scrutiny stemming from alleged improprieties by bond underwriting firms doing business with the County.

"The ongoing SEC investigation of Smith Barney regarding transactions with Dade County placed a 'cloud' over the firm, much like the 'cloud' cited by the Metro Commission when it voted to exclude two smaller, minority-owned firms -- Grigsby & Associates and Leo Guzman & Company," Penelas said. "It is in the public interest that there be a level playing field in Dade County's bond program."

"We have the opportunity to send a strong, clear message to both Dade County taxpayers and the financial markets that Dade County government is committed to cleaning up its bond business," Penelas said.
